summary: Frontend-only retest of citation fix + summary regression on /chat. BOTH scenarios PASS. (1) Acme query 'Show me Acme invoices from March over 5,000': LLM this time emitted '[#1][#2]' (one bracket per citation per prompt update). splitCitations produced both citation segments, and chat-citation-1 and chat-citation-2 chips rendered inline. Clicking chat-citation-1 scrolled and applied amber ring (bg-amber-100 ring-2 ring-amber-400) to chat-reference-row-0; clicking chat-citation-2 highlighted chat-reference-row-1. References table (chat-references-table) shows 2 rows with headers ['#','Date','Supplier','Name','Type','Amount']. (2) Monthly summary regression: chat-summary-table renders 3 month-total rows: 2026-03 Total $540.74 (Umbrella Supplies $450.75, Office Depot $89.99), 2026-01 Total $120.00 (Globex), 2025-11 Total $2,300.00 (Wayne Enterprises) — all values match the expected set exactly. Also verified: splitCitations now resiliently expands grouped '[#1, #2]' and ranges '[#1-#3]' into individual segments (code reviewed in /app/lib/chat/citations.ts), so even if the LLM regresses to grouped form, chips will still render. Prompt instruction + parser both updated — defense in depth.
critical_code_review_comments: lib/chat/citations.ts: nice defense-in-depth — regex /\[#\s*(\d+(?:\s*[,\-]\s*#?\s*\d+)*)\]/g plus expandIndices covers single, comma-grouped, and range forms. Guard b-a<100 prevents accidental huge ranges — good.
components/chat/chat-view.tsx AnswerText: out-of-range citation index gracefully falls back to plain text — correct.
Consider adding a one-line unit test for splitCitations covering '[#1][#2]', '[#1, #2]', '[#1-#3]' to lock in behavior.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_3 bug (missing citation chips on grouped tokens) is resolved. Both prompt and parser were updated. Verified via live Claude run on preview /chat. All required data-testids present and working: chat-citation-1/2, chat-reference-row-0/1, chat-references-table, chat-summary-table, chat-summary-month-total-0..2.
